It is a game of high tension and strategic risk-taking where players capture floral cards representing the 12 months to form specific combinations (Jokbo). The game is famous for the 'Go' or 'Stop' decision, where a winning player can choose to risk their points to double them or stop immediately to secure victory.
Derived from the Japanese Hanafuda deck introduced to Korea in the late 19th century. Koreans adapted the rules, significantly increasing the complexity and adding the signature 'Go/Stop' mechanic.
48 cards (12 months x 4 cards each) + optional 2-5 bonus/joker cards.
